transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
Well, once I start eating my comfort foods, I have a hard time stopping. I tell myself, “Maria, that’s enough,” but I still keep reaching back into the pot. It feels like I can’t make myself stop.
When this happens, do you eat an unusually large amount of food for the situation?

Yes. Some afternoons after choir or working in the garden, I’ll have a plate of rice and beans or chicken stew, then keep going back for more. By the time I stop, I’ve eaten what could’ve been two or three meals.
After you eat this way, do you ever make yourself vomit?
No, I don’t make myself vomit after I eat.
After you eat this way, do you ever try to make up for it by exercising a lot?
I’m not sure what you mean by exercising a lot. I do my usual things, but I don’t really think of it as making up for eating.
After you eat this way, do you ever use laxatives or water pills to try to make up for it?
I’m not really sure what you mean by water pills. I haven’t noticed myself doing anything like that to make up for it.
When this happens, does it feel like you cannot control how much you eat or when you stop eating?
Yes. Once I start on those comfort foods, I’ll tell myself, “Maria, that’s enough,” but I keep reaching back into the pot. It feels like I can’t make myself stop.
Do these episodes of overeating upset you a lot?
Yes, I do. Afterward I feel ashamed and sad. It’s like I took something that used to mean family and caring and turned it into something I have to hide from the people at church.
How often do these overeating episodes happen?
Since my friend passed, it’s been most weeks—usually once or twice, in those quiet afternoons after choir or gardening.
